Subject: FinLedger SLA carveout request — APAC replication window & RPO

Hi Daniel,

Thanks again for walking through the deployment plan yesterday. Following internal review, FinLedger’s compliance group has asked us to document a temporary SLA carveout for the APAC tenant while we finish the cross-region replication improvements. Specifically they want explicit language around:

- RTO and RPO expectations during the 90-day stabilization window;
- What fallback behaviors Redwood will take if APAC writes cannot replicate within the primary-standby window;
- Any financial credits or incident remediation commitments tied to missed RTO/RPO;
- Data residency/replication endpoints during the interim.

We proposed a conservative interim profile to be explicit and actionable:

- RTO (region failover): 15 minutes for control-plane failovers, 60 minutes for full warm-standby switchover requiring rehydration;
- RPO (data loss tolerance): up to 30 minutes for the APAC tenant while async replication buffering is enabled;

Attachments: I’ve included a draft carveout clause (finledger-sla-draft-20261109.pdf) and a CSV of recent replication metrics (replication-metrics-apac.csv) showing tail latency and lag patterns.

Request: can you confirm these interim tolerances are acceptable to FinLedger’s risk/compliance? If not, please call out which requirements are non-negotiable and we’ll route to engineering & legal for a formal redline.

Next steps from our side: I’m looping Karthik and Irene to propose mitigation controls (prefetch windows, prefix caching, and an emergency synchronous fallback for the narrow set of customer-critical keys). Marissa will coordinate how this maps to your contract amendment if we need to formalize.

Thanks — Naomi

Naomi,

Appreciate the thoroughness. A few clarifying points from our side after review with compliance and our platform team:

1) RPO 30 minutes is higher than our baseline objective for financial transactions — we need a justification for why synchronous replication is not viable during this window.
2) The proposed 60-minute switchover for full warm-standby sounds long for our critical flows (we’d expect <30). Is the extra time primarily rehydration of cache and indexes?
3) We will need a clear rollback/fallback playbook if failover completes but customer-facing consistency is degraded — who owns the rollback decision and what are SLAs for remediation?

We’re open to an interim carveout if you can: (a) justify the async RPO technically; (b) offer compensatory controls (e.g., increased monitoring, alert thresholds, playbook with on-call SRE contact); and (c) include a limited credit schedule if unacceptable data loss occurs.

Please get us a technical note we can share with our compliance team.

Thanks,
Daniel

Thanks, Naomi. Quick technical note for Daniel and the FinLedger team — TL;DR below, longer rationale and mitigations after.

TL;DR: APAC currently runs async cross-region replication into our warm-standby in us-west. The primary constraint is write amplification and tail-latency on nightly batch jobs that can temporarily spike replication lag. Full synchronous replication across intercontinental links would reduce RPO to near-zero but would introduce 2–3x write latency on peak flows and a higher failure blast radius. For trading/financial ledgers that need sub-second durability we recommend:

- Short-term: keep async replication but reduce RPO to 15 minutes for critical keyspaces using an opt-in sync-like path we can enable per-customer;
- Medium-term (30–90 days): enable prefix-level synchronous mirroring for the 10% of keys you mark as high-criticality (no global sync required);
- Operational mitigations we’ll implement immediately: active lag monitoring with push alerts at 60s/120s thresholds, auto-fallback to a read-only degraded mode for non-critical reads, and an on-call SRE escalation list for any >15m sustained lag.

Details and why we picked numbers:
- The 60-minute full switchover number Naomi referenced assumes a cold index rebuild for some auxiliary services; removing auxiliary rebuilds drops that to ~20–30 minutes in practice. We can publish a trimmed switchover plan that targets 25–30 minutes for customer-impacting flows.
- For RPO, the default async path has historically sat between 2–8 minutes under nominal load, but spikes during nightly processing have produced 20–40 minute outliers — hence our conservative 30-minute ask. With prefix-level sync for critical keys we can get to <=15 minutes guaranteed.

Attachments: I’ve attached the APAC replication diagram that shows where we can add the per-customer sync path. apac-replication-architecture-diagram.png

Proposed contractual language snippet (for legal):
"During the stated stabilization window (90 days), Redwood will maintain a best-effort RPO of 15 minutes for customer-designated critical keyspaces and an RPO of up to 30 minutes for non-designated keys. Redwood will provide 24/7 monitoring and a documented escalation/playbook; in the event of RPO breach exceeding the designated tolerance for >30 minutes for critical keyspaces, Redwood will provide a service credit equal to X% of monthly fees for the impacted service, subject to customer claim and verification."

We’re open to firming the credit language and the exact X% with Marissa and legal based on your procurement needs.

-Karthik

Hi Daniel — following up with a consolidated proposal that tries to balance FinLedger’s risk posture and Redwood’s operational constraints. Key points below and an action list for sign-off.

Summary proposal (seek your OK):
- Term: 90-day stabilization carveout, starting upon mutual signature of the amendment;
- RPO: 15 minutes guaranteed for customer-designated critical keyspaces (we will work with you to label these), up to 30 minutes for non-designated keys;
- RTO / switchover: Target 25–30 minutes for customer-facing services; 60 minutes for full-service rehydration of auxiliary systems;
- Controls: 24/7 active lag monitoring with push alerts, per-customer on-call escalation (we’ll share SRE rotation contact), and an emergency synchronous path enabled for up to 10% of keys;
- Credits: For verified RPO breach on designated critical keyspaces >30 minutes, Redwood will offer a service credit scaled by impact (starting proposal: 5% of monthly fees for the impacted service per qualifying incident, capped at 50% monthly). Full credit schedule to be finalized with procurement.

Action items:
1) FinLedger to confirm acceptance of the RPO/RTO numbers and the credit framework (reply with any redlines).
2) Naomi/Marissa to route the amendment to Redwood legal; Karthik & team to publish the trimmed switchover runbook.
3) Schedule a 45-minute run-through with your compliance and platform (we can do next week) to show monitoring and the emergency sync path.

If you can confirm by EOD Tuesday we’ll move the amendment to DocuSign and schedule the technical walkthrough. Appreciate the candid feedback — we want to make sure the failure modes are explicit and the remediation commitments are actionable.

Best,
Naomi
